title: Set up a business phone number
summary: Get the company a phone number that is not a founder's cell: choose the provider type, pick or port the number, complete the identity and messaging registrations the destination country requires, configure routing and voicemail, and record the number everywhere the company contact phone lives.

parts.title: Choose the business-phone provider
parts.guidance: Decide who answers before choosing a provider: a team answering shared lines wants a business-phone system with ring groups, voicemail, and a shared message inbox; software answering or dialing wants a programmable telephony API. Compare the shortlisted providers on the team features the chosen type needs — the shared text inbox, ring groups and business-hours routing, voicemail transcription, and CRM integrations — plus number coverage in the countries you need, messaging support, and what the provider exposes to agents and automation. Record the choice and the plan; the number purchase and the compliance registrations happen inside this account.

options.title: Default — shared business-phone system
options.summary: A business-phone system the team answers: shared numbers, ring groups, business hours, voicemail transcription, and a shared text inbox. The right default when humans handle the calls and texts and the company wants the number off personal devices.

execution.rationale: The company owner compares shared-line features, country coverage and plan terms through provider information and remote discussion, then records the team's service choice.

options.title: Programmable telephony API
options.summary: A programmable platform that exposes number provisioning, voice, and messaging as APIs. The right choice when software answers — IVRs, support automations, or agents place and receive the traffic — or when telephony is being built into the product itself.
options.when: Software, not a team, answers or dials: telephony built into the product or run by agents

execution.rationale: The technical owner compares the programmable providers against the intended product and records the platform choice digitally; selecting an API service does not itself execute its provisioning or calling operations.

parts.title: Pick the number
parts.guidance: Choose the number the company will publish. Check the exact number's voice and messaging capability before buying — not every number supports SMS — and confirm the monthly and usage charges on the provider's published pricing. Where the destination country requires identity or address documentation before a number there can be purchased, complete the next step's business-identity bundle first and come back; US numbers purchase immediately. If the company already has a number people know, port it instead of buying a new one; the port branch has its own paperwork and timing.

options.title: Default — new local number
options.summary: Buy a new number local to where the company operates or sells. Search the provider's inventory for the area code and confirm the number supports both voice and messaging where texting is planned. Complete the purchase — or, where the destination country gates purchase on identity documents, reserve the choice and finish the purchase once the next step's documentation is accepted. Record the number, its capabilities, and its line item on the plan.

execution.rationale: An authorized operator checks the selected provider's inventory, capabilities, charges and identity prerequisites, then purchases the approved local number through the account interface and records it.

options.title: Toll-free number
options.summary: A toll-free number reads as a national presence and keeps callers from paying for the call. Where texting is planned, check the country's rules first: in some markets a toll-free number cannot send SMS until a verification is approved, so the messaging-registration step gates the first text.
options.when: A national presence matters more than a local area code

execution.rationale: The account owner selects and purchases the toll-free number through the chosen provider's interface, checking country coverage and the separate verification required before texting.

options.title: Vanity number
options.summary: A memorable digit pattern or word-mapped number. Search the provider's inventory for the pattern, expect fewer matches and sometimes a premium, and apply the same voice-and-messaging capability check before buying.
options.when: The number itself is marketing: a memorable pattern worth the search

execution.rationale: The account owner searches the provider's number inventory for the desired pattern, checks capabilities and any premium, and completes the approved purchase through the account interface.

options.title: Port an existing number
options.summary: Keep the number the company already answers. Gather the losing carrier's account number, PIN, and billing details exactly as that carrier holds them, sign the letter of authorization, and schedule the port. Keep the old service active until the port completes — cancelling early can forfeit the number — and expect the timeline to vary by country and carrier.
options.when: The company already has a number customers know

references.title: Twilio docs: Port a number in

execution.rationale: The account owner supplies the carrier records and personally signs the port authorization, then coordinates the transfer and tracks its status digitally while keeping the old service active.

parts.title: Complete the business identity the provider and country require
parts.guidance: Fill in the provider's business profile with the company's legal name, registered address, and contact details exactly as the company's registrations state them. Many countries require identity or proof-of-address documentation before a number there can be purchased or activated, so check the destination country's requirements and supply the documents up front. Mismatches between the profile and the company's registered details are the usual cause of rejected registrations downstream.

references.title: Twilio docs: Regulatory compliance for phone numbers

execution.rationale: The authorized representative reconciles company identity records and supplies the selected provider's required profile and supporting documents through its account process; personal verification remains with that representative.

parts.title: Complete the messaging registrations the destination country requires before texting
parts.guidance: Where the company plans to text, complete the country's sender registrations before the first production message, using the business identity from the previous step. Unregistered application traffic gets filtered and surcharged where registration regimes exist, so treat the registration review time as part of the setup, document the opt-in and opt-out flows the registration asks about, and wait for approved status before pointing campaigns at the number.

verify.how: The provider's compliance console shows the brand, campaign, and number registrations in an approved state before the first production message; retain the registration records with the account details.

geoResolutions.label: Register the A2P 10DLC brand and campaign before texting from a 10-digit local number, and complete toll-free verification before SMS on a toll-free number
geoResolutions.guidance: US carriers require application-to-person traffic on 10-digit local numbers to be registered — unregistered traffic is filtered and carries extra carrier fees — and a toll-free number cannot send SMS to the US or Canada until its verification is approved.

execution.rationale: The account owner completes the applicable sender registrations in the selected provider's compliance service, answers review questions and confirms approval before production texting.

parts.title: Configure call routing, voicemail, and the shared inbox
parts.guidance: Set the business hours, the ring order or group that answers inside them, and the after-hours behavior. Record or generate the voicemail greeting, turn on voicemail transcription to email or chat where the plan carries it, and set forwarding for the people who take calls on the move. Put texts and voicemails in a shared inbox so responders see one another's replies, then test the whole path from an outside line: open hours, closed hours, voicemail, and a text.

execution.rationale: The phone administrator configures the actual service and shared inbox digitally, then checks open-hours routing, after-hours routing, voicemail and messaging from an outside line; the full provider-specific setup and test remain human-operated.

parts.title: Record the number everywhere the company contact phone lives
parts.guidance: Update every place that holds the company's contact phone: the website and contact pages, the bank and card accounts, the payment processor profile and its statement descriptor, business registrations and directories, email signatures, and the hiring-paperwork templates that print an employer phone. Keep one canonical record of the number and its owner so later changes propagate from a single place.

geoResolutions.label: Put the number on the US paperwork that asks for an employer phone: bank and processor KYC profiles, and the written notice New York employers give at hire, which must state the employer's telephone number (law rule us-ny.wage-notice-at-hire)

execution.rationale: The administrator updates the phone number in the actual website, financial accounts, directories, signatures and employment templates, checking each service's access requirements and maintaining the ownership record.

links.when: Texting is planned on the number; voice-only setups skip the messaging registrations.
Voice-only setup: no messaging registrations to wait on, straight to routing.

metadata.supportReason: Number search, purchase, and routing configuration are API surfaces at the programmable providers; the identity and messaging registrations are review queues fed with human-supplied business details.

contextNeeded.query: business identity details (legal name, registered address, website)
